extracted.intended_audience: researchers and clinicians designing, validating, or using clinical/diagnostic/observational measurement instruments and conducting interrater reliability studies
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, implementing, and reporting interrater reliability, instrument validation, and diagnostic-accuracy studies (clinical, imaging, observational tools). Includes development/adaptation of scales, training procedures, choice of reliability statistics, and interpretation guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: MRI-based crack/fracture imaging criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: MRI-based criteria for crack/fracture appearance were defined as 1-2 sharply-delineated, high-signal (bright/white) line shape(s) that must be visible on multiple contiguous image slices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The line shape(s) must present as single entities, or parallel pairs in close proximity, or pairs in close proximity exhibiting convergence or divergence extending from the external boundary of the tooth to the pulpal cavity. These imaging appearance rules were developed by an MRI physicist and dentists and used as the reference for reader training and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report diagnostic accuracy with sensitivity/specificity and confidence intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Report sensitivity and specificity for diagnostic tests with 95% confidence intervals and pre-specified significance level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Sensitivity: MRI = 0.59 (95% CI: 0.39-0.76; p = 0.46); Specificity: MRI = 0.83 (95% CI: 0.64-0.94; p < 0.01). Statistical significance threshold used: alpha ≤ 0.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Cohen's kappa and interpretation via Landis & Koch
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure agreement using Cohen's kappa and judge levels of agreement using the criteria of Landis and Koch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Landis & Koch interpretation categories (commonly referenced) are used to classify kappa values (e.g., slight, fair, moderate, substantial, almost perfect) when reporting observer agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select and report appropriate interrater reliability statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose and report reliability estimators appropriate to data type: Cohen's kappa, weighted kappa, Fleiss' kappa, intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), percent agreement, prevalence- and bias-adjusted kappa (PABAK), Pearson/Spearman, generalizability coefficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several studies used Cohen's kappa (κ), weighted κ for ordinal scales, Fleiss' κ for multi-rater categorical data, ICC for continuous measures, and percent agreement. Always report confidence intervals (e.g., 95% CI) with the reliability estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and standardized rater procedures to improve reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide rater training and standardized protocols/definitions before data collection to improve intra- and inter-rater reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: MRI criteria developed and a training period preceded blinded rating; pilot training program used to determine reliability for photographic grading scales; video education improved knowledge though raters requested additional interaction. Training is emphasized as necessary when reliabilities are suboptimal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop rating-scale items using face validity and test-retest studies
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating items to measure guideline/content compliance, assess face validity with focus groups and perform test-retest reliability studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example procedure: conduct focus groups to evaluate face validity and feasibility, then perform test-retest with participants rating the same materials at two time points; compute correlations (r, rho) and kappa statistics to assess stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative multi-step development and double-abstraction sampling for data abstraction tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop abstraction tools iteratively and test reliability via independent double abstraction on a random sample of records with predetermined sampling fractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: compute Cohen's kappa for preliminary and finalized tools; for n=1440 cases, 108 cases (10% of first half sample; 5% of last half sample) were independently re-abstracted to assess reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create photographic/visual grading scales with pilot training and define minimally perceivable difference
rubrics_metrics.description: Design grading scales using standardized photographic panels, run pilot training to establish reliability, and define a minimally perceivable difference (MCID) on the scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a 6-point Grading Scale (GGS) created by copying photographed wrinkles onto a control image; a pilot training program determined reliability (weighted κ 0.85–0.86). Investigators considered a score difference of 0.5 to be a minimally perceivable difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize indicators via Delphi and assess feasibility with explicit reliability thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Use expert consensus (e.g., modified Delphi) to prioritize quality indicators, then pilot-test feasibility and reliability with explicit thresholds for acceptable indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example thresholds: indicators considered feasible if observed agreement >95% and adjusted kappa index >0.6 or non-adjusted kappa index >0.6 for composites and components. Indicators failing thresholds require refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and cross-cultural adaptation procedure for instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow a standard multi-step process for translation and cross-cultural adaptation: forward translation, synthesis of translations, back translation, expert committee review, and testing of a pre-final version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After adaptation, evaluate measurement properties (reliability, intra/inter-rater agreement) and report coefficients (e.g., Linear Weighted Kappa) with 95% CIs and cross-tabulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate instrument structure and concurrent validity with established measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess construct validity via factor analysis and concurrent validity by comparing with established instruments/tests relevant to the construct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: perform factor analysis (report % variance explained), test interrater reliability (κ/ICC), and compare with SF-36, 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT), or disease-specific scores (HOOS) to demonstrate concurrent validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-specify and use reliability interpretation thresholds (ICC/kappa ranges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use accepted interpretive ranges for reliability coefficients and report category-level exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from studies: ICC > 0.74 = excellent; ICC 0.60–0.74 = good; kappa categories per Landis & Koch. Also some validation studies considered lower 95% confidence limit >0.4 as acceptable for certain indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use known-groups comparison for construct validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess construct validity by comparing scores between groups known to differ on the construct (known-groups method).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: store scores used to compare venues expected to differ in nutrition environment to establish construct validity of NEMS-GG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design scale formats matched to perceptual tasks (equal-appearing intervals, bipolar semantic scales)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select scale format appropriate to the perceptual judgment: equally appearing interval scales for global grade and multi-point bipolar semantic scales for tonal or affective dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Overall Grade' rated on a 0–3 equally appearing interval scale and 'Neoglottal Tonicity' on an 11-point bipolar semantic scale; use weighted κ for ordinal scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not equate rater confidence with reliability; measure objective agreement for each feature
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect rater confidence but assess objective agreement separately (feature-level multirater kappa), since high confidence can coexist with low reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: In hypsarrhythmia assessment raters reported high confidence despite κ values indicating poor agreement on many EEG features. Report κ for each rated feature (voltage, disorganization, epileptiform discharges, slowing, symmetry, synchrony, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify testing protocols and movement/task conditions for physical assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Define standardized test maneuvers and conditions for physical classification assessments to increase reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: For scapular dyskinesis classification, assess subjects during bilateral arm raising/lowering with a weighted load in the scapular plane and classify patterns I–IV; report agreement separately for raising and lowering phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define ordinal category labels and test–retest intervals for manual clinical scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear category definitions for manual assessment tools and include test–retest timing in reliability studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Sternal Instability Scale (SIS) uses 4 categories from 0 (clinically stable) to 3 (separated sternum with overriding); reliability study used two assessments 48 hours apart and reported κ for intra- and inter-rater reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine quantitative reliability assessment with qualitative evaluation of training interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating educational interventions (e.g., video training), assess knowledge gain, interrater reliability, and collect qualitative feedback on the training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: nurses watched an educational video, completed knowledge tests, performed parallel assessments with a researcher, and were interviewed; interrater reliability measured with weighted κ and confidence limits; participants requested additional interaction beyond video.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute and report content validity indices and internal-consistency metrics for questionnaires
rubrics_metrics.description: For self-report questionnaires, report item-level content validity index (I-CVI), scale-level content validity index (S-CVI), Cronbach's alpha for internal consistency, percent observed agreement, and weighted kappa for inter-rater comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: PAQ-C and PAQ-A reported I-CVI ranges, S-CVI ~0.89–0.90, Cronbach's α ≈ 0.76–0.78, percent agreement ranges for items, and weighted κ ranges ~0.48–0.69.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use convergent validity with established clinical scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate convergent validity by correlating new instrument scores with established clinical scales that measure related constructs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: CANFOR Portuguese convergent validity assessed using Global Assessment of Functioning (GAF) and Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS) scores; significant correlations support validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: List and rate component features when instrument measures multi-dimensional phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Break down complex phenomena into discrete features and report reliability per feature rather than only a global judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: EEG hypsarrhythmia assessment rated features such as voltage, organization, epileptiform discharges, slowing, interictal attenuations, symmetry, synchrony—κ reported for each feature to identify which are reliable and which are not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess classification system accuracy and explore predictors of coding disagreement
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating categorical classification systems (e.g., fracture classification), measure accuracy and reliability (proportion agreement, κ) and analyze factors associated with poor coding agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: AO/OTA classification study reported intrarater and interrater κ ≈ 0.67 and used logistic regression to identify predictors of accuracy (fracture type, frequency, segment fractured). Report overall agreement (PA) alongside κ.
